source.title: Shortcut Before Circuit: Document Statistics Time In-Context Conflict Resolution

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports delayed formation of a retrieval circuit and measures when its readout becomes meaningful, but its main refinement is that the training objective cannot identify which of two coextensive rules is implemented. It also finds substantial seed- and schedule-dependent variation in that readout.
record.gate_note: The study uses a synthetic in-context assignment task with an infinite training stream, not a small fixed algorithmic dataset exhibiting train–test overfitting. Generator-only candidate-rule collision rates and cited results are not model-result rows. The non-queried-slot control edit, covariate analyses, and geometry attempt are noted in the text but do not measure the versions’ named outcomes. The main grid’s 75 runs all end in the retrieval state; the excluded Rold=2 results are not included as rows here.
record.test_reason: This study does not test any version of the grokking claim. The training stream is infinite and train and test share one distribution. There is no memorization phase and no gap between train and test performance, so no delayed generalization occurs. What it studies is a plateau on a positional shortcut followed by abrupt acquisition of an in-context retrieval circuit. That is abrupt learning in the style of induction-head formation. It cites Power et al. and Nanda et al. only as examples of phase diagrams. Its loss-derivative peak is a feature of the same training loss, not a hidden progress measure of a generalizing circuit replacing memorization. Its seed-variance result concerns rules the objective cannot distinguish (recency vs rarity) in a non-grokking setting. The intervention readout is explicitly not an algorithm identifier, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. Recency and rarity are coextensive by construction, so the objective is indifferent between them. Per-cell rule readouts do not replicate across seeds, checkpoints, schedules or depth. Escape timing from a positional shortcut with a closed-form ceiling does replicate and is monotone in redundancy. The authors add that gating on circuit formation is necessary but not sufficient, and that the corpus fixes when a mechanism appears, not which one.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains 26.1M-parameter transformers on an infinite synthetic in-context assignment stream and probes an input-edit rule readout. It does not reproduce small-dataset modular arithmetic grokking or the original studies’ training/test-accuracy procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcomes varying with seed, redundancy Rold, schedule length, model depth, and—in a limited arm—initial QK-normalization gain. The main finding is that per-cell rule readouts vary across seeds and checkpoints; escape timing is ordered by redundancy in the tested grid.

fits_no_version.finding: Models plateau for thousands of steps on a positional shortcut with a closed-form ceiling, then abruptly acquire retrieval. Escape step is monotone in redundancy Rold, and a loss-derivative peak precedes the copy-diagnostic gate by a few hundred steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abrupt shortcut-to-circuit transitions in in-context tasks on infinite data, with timing set by corpus statistics (plateau or abrupt learning, not grokking).

fits_no_version.finding: Under a multiplicity-inversion edit, the per-cell rule readout varies widely across seeds: range up to 0.879 against a 0.025 standard error. It also varies across checkpoints, schedule length and depth, while all runs reach ≥0.999 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When two rules are coextensive on the training data, which rule a network implements is underdetermined and varies across runs. This relates to, but is not, V6's algorithm-convergence question for grokked networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Halving the initial QK-norm gain (γ=2 to γ=1) prevents circuit formation within 16000 steps at Rold=3 but not at Rold=16 (App. B.1). An earlier dataloader bug that replayed a fixed document set produced an apparent abrupt transition driven by memorization (App. A.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale gates abrupt circuit formation; data replay can manufacture apparent phase transitions.

record.problems: One synthetic language and one primary architecture family; no non-aliased control construction. The rule readout is explicitly not a unique mechanism identifier, and it varies across seeds, checkpoints, schedules, and depth. Several covariates are collinear and not fully isolated. The loss-derivative peak is affected by schedule decay in some runs; schedule and depth arms have limited coverage. The study does not test the small-dataset train–test overfitting pattern in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Generator-only statistics, the filler-slot edit control, and the geometry test reported as uninformative are described in gate_note rather than extracted as claim-version results.

untested.parts: No fixed small dataset, no train-test gap, no dependence on dataset size.
No Fourier or generalizing circuit versus memorization; no measurement of memorizing components being removed.
No non-algorithmic data and no lazy-to-rich manipulation of a grokking delay.
No weight-decay manipulation, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No algorithm identification in grokked networks.
No test of optimizer or softmax numerical artifacts creating a delay.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' classification is overridden. The study never measures generalization delayed beyond a training-fit, since it uses an infinite stream with the same train and test distribution. Grokking papers appear only as cited examples of phase diagrams. The V2 'challenges' label on R1 was also unfounded: the authors explicitly warn that the coarse-grid abruptness may be a thresholding artifact.

versions.untested_parts: No small fixed training dataset or train–test accuracy trajectory is tested; the training stream is infinite. The paper does not test chance test accuracy after training accuracy saturates or delay as a function of training-set size.

It measures a retrieval/copy diagnostic and a loss-derivative peak, not a Fourier circuit for modular arithmetic. It does not test gradual formation of Fourier components or later removal of memorizing components.

The task is synthetic and algorithmic; the study does not test images, text corpora, molecules, or a lazy-to-rich transition. A QK-normalization initial-gain arm is not a test of the stated broad regime claim.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test whether weight decay favors an efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.

The intervention reads out dependence on multiplicity, but the authors caution that it separates a family of mechanisms rather than identifying a unique algorithm. The study does not establish the specific algorithms used in individual runs.

The study checks deterministic reruns and schedule sensitivity of the rule readout, but does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts create and remove the delayed-generalization behavior in V7.

rows.subject: 75-run main grid, 26.1M-parameter decoder-only transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the copy diagnostic on held-out task documents over training; reported the transition for escaping cells.
rows.value: In every escaping cell, the diagnostic moves from near chance to above 0.95 between consecutive evaluations.
rows.note: The reported transition is abrupt on the evaluation grid, rather than gradual circuit formation. The paper cautions that this thresholded diagnostic alone does not locate the reorganization.
rows.check: Copy-diagnostic jump at shortcut escape is not train-test delayed generalization; no memorizing component. 'reversed' against V2 is unwarranted, since the authors say a coarse gate can manufacture abruptness.

rows.subject: 75-run main grid, 26.1M-parameter decoder-only transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured sequence accuracy as models escaped the positional shortcut.
rows.value: Jumps from the positional ceiling to 1.000 as the copy diagnostic leaves chance; all 75 runs reach accuracy ≥0.999 at the final checkpoint.
rows.note: This is a shortcut-to-retrieval transition, not a reported train–test grokking curve. The study does not report training accuracy saturation preceding test accuracy.
rows.check: Accuracy jump from the positional ceiling to 1.000 on the training distribution, with no train-test gap; not a grokking measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The unthresholded loss-derivative peak precedes the copy-diagnostic gate, providing a progress measure before the reported transition (R3–R7).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The copy diagnostic is reported to jump from near chance to above 0.95 between evaluations, rather than showing gradual circuit formation (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Aliased-rule multiplicity-inversion readouts across seeds, checkpoints, schedules, and depths
reader_labels.reason: The readout varies substantially across seeds and can move with checkpoints, schedule, or depth; the authors explicitly decline to assign a unique mechanism to individual cells, so these results do not establish a common identifiable algorithm (R8–R23).
